newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil stocks end up in nervous seesaw session.
newsitem.headline: Brazil stocks end up in nervous seesaw session.

text.p: Brazilian stocks closed higher in a seesaw session marked by investor jitters regarding a possible Congressional vote on civil service reform and telecoms rumors, brokers said.
"The market was nervous today," said one local trader. "It opened firm, then went down, then rose again at the end."
The bolsa's Bovespa index of 49 most-traded shares closed 0.84 percent higher at 9,819 points in moderately strong trade of 768.9 million reais ($725.4 million).

Brokers said shares were smartly higher in the morning, led by hikes in telecommunications stocks after the government unveiled an incentives package Monday for cellular equipment imports to aid an expected boom in the sector.

But uncertainty over whether Congress' lower house would vote on a government civil service reform bill and rumors of a legal challange to a B Band cellular phone concession kept investors on edge, they said.
Wednesday's rise was led by benchmark blue chip Telebras, whose preferred share rose 0.99 percent to close at 122.50 reais.

Other strong risers were retailer Casa Anglo, which surged 8.19 percent to close at 46.52 reais, and Ericsson Telecomunicaoes, which ended up 6.34 percent at 36.90 reais on the cellular incentives package.
Among blue chip gainers, state mining firm Companhia Vale do Rio Doce preferred climbed 0.6 percent to end at 25.25 reais, and state oil firm Petrobras rose 1.41 percent to close at 215.50 reais.
The bolsa's Electrical Energy Index ended 0.45 percent higher at 2,702 points, including a 1.4 percent hike in federal power firm Eletrobras, which ended at 508 reais.
The power sector index was led by Sao Paulo state power distributor CPFL preferred, which rose 3.46 percent to 150.00 reais.
State power firm Cesp preferred bucked the trend to end 0.17 percent lower, while Minas Gerais state electric firm Cemig preferred moved up 0.19 percent to close at 48.29 reais.
